title: The Sodder Children: Gone on Christmas Eve
sources: Smithsonian (Karen Abbott) via Doe Network: Christmas Eve 1945, Fayetteville WV; George and Jennie Sodder and nine of their ten children at home; Fire Chief F.J. Morris and the 'phone tree'; billboard on Route 16 for nearly four decades
The Clio: around 1:00 a.m. Dec 25 1945 the house was in flames; four of nine children escaped; fire department only 2.5 miles away; no signs of the children found in the ashes
Postcard History / The Line Up: fire department did not arrive until about 7 a.m.; missing ladder, trucks that would not start, dead phone line; official cause faulty wiring
The Collector: authorities found the phone line had been cut
Strange Outdoors: billboard stayed up until shortly after Jennie Sodder died in 1989
The Line Up: the five children were Maurice, Martha, Louis, Jennie and Betty, aged 5 to 14; official explanation is that they died in the fire

lines.text: On Christmas Eve, 1945, in a small West Virginia town,
lines.caps: On | Christmas | Eve, | 1945,~nineteen | in a | small | West | Virginia | town,

lines.text: the Sodder family went to bed,
with nine of their ten children at home.
lines.caps: with | 9~nine | of their | 10~ten | children | at home.

lines.text: But around one in the morning,
their house caught fire.
The parents and four of the kids got out,
but five of them never came out.
And that night, everything went wrong.
The phone line was dead,
the ladder was missing,
and the trucks wouldn't start.
The fire station was just two and a half miles away,
lines.caps: The | fire | station | was just | 2.5~two | miles | away,

lines.text: but help didn't come until seven in the morning.
lines.caps: but | help | didn't | come | until | 7 AM.~seven

lines.text: By then, the house was ash.
Officials said the five children died in the fire,
but no remains were ever found.
So their parents never stopped searching.
They put up a billboard by the highway,
and it stood there for almost forty years.
lines.caps: and it | stood | there | for | almost | 40 years.~forty

lines.text: Now, more than eighty years later,
nobody knows what really happened to the Sodder children.
So... were they lost in the fire, or taken that night?
